long_biography.plain_text:
At CFC, Andy Holmes has argued that routine insurance transactions should occupy less of an underwriter’s day. He favours using automated systems for straightforward risks, leaving staff more time to develop relationships with brokers and customers. Data can also help identify businesses whose needs make them suitable prospects for cover.

He applied a similarly practical approach to attracting insurance capital. CFC’s Lloyd’s syndicate gave investors a route into an established book of small-business risks. Designed without its own permanent underwriting-room presence or dedicated staff, the syndicate drew on the wider company’s existing portfolio and operating infrastructure.
